object_description: slim two-storey block set at right angles to the existing school, with a small equipment cube outside
geometry_property: at right angles to the existing school
design_condition: the block is placed at right angles to the existing school building, departing slightly from the neighbouring building line, so that its slimness generates a generous amount of open space on both sides

positive: A careful reading of the site gives a clear statement about location, orientation and size
The perpendicular arrangement makes the spatial and content-related connection to the existing buildings tangible
The slim structure generates a generous amount of open space
The positioning offers an appropriate entrance area on one side and a spacious garden on the other
Using the topography, different entrances and exits connect the building with the open space
The simple design of the open space gives the children plenty of scope
The play meadow can be interpreted as a common outdoor space between the public buildings
The existing site edge is supplemented by a berm path belonging exclusively to the new facility
The large green space is read as a forest clearing and a changing colour space where children can stay safely
The path along the forest edge connects this quiet space with the urban anteroom to the south-west
This urban space forms an overall unit yet enables individual addresses for the parts of the house
The exposed playing field with a central shading tree contrasts with the introverted clearing
This contrast could become an interesting spatial experience for the children, and the meadow is a land reserve
The equipment room forms a counterpoint to the main body in form and content
It becomes the centre where three different outdoor areas overlap
The small cube stands on the border between foreign and own area for the child
The small footprint and compact structure take up little land and require little earth movement
The regularly timed concrete framework allows the room to be divided as freely as possible
The support spacing makes static sense and is appropriately dimensioned for the programme
All interior walls except the core are reversible in position, opening type and composition
The room sequence and circulation in the day care area can therefore be varied
Ground floor kindergarten rooms run through the depth, lit and accessible from both sides
Regular skylights direct light evenly across the ceiling into the middle rooms
Serving rooms pass daylight on to the access area, which is kept bright
The vertical connection sits discreetly without interrupting the consistent rhythm of the block
A very flexible and spatially interesting structure allowing various spatial constellations
Its compact mass and low height allow regular illumination
The house and interiors convey a friendly, cheerful atmosphere
negative: The direct connection between the new building and the play meadow is deliberately avoided
Not all dimensions of the spatial programme are adhered to because the grid was defined too narrowly
The proposed transparency prevents the quiet, rather closed room zones necessary for operation
